title: Term 1 and 2 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 1 and 2.
This question paper consists of 6 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.
Show your working, and round your answers as each question asks.

questions.prompt: What does the M in IDMEC stand for?
Classify each statement as a specification or a constraint.

pairs.left: Must be completed in two weeks
Must hold at least 2 litres of water
Only recycled materials may be used
Must fit inside a school bag

questions.prompt: Give THREE questions you could ask when analysing an existing product.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): What is its purpose? Who uses it? What materials are used? How is it made? Is it safe? What does it cost? How could it be improved? What is its impact on the environment?

questions.prompt: Which type of line shows edges that cannot be seen?
At what angle to the horizontal are horizontal edges drawn in isometric drawing?
In first-angle orthographic projection, the top view is drawn…
options: to the left of the front view

questions.prompt: In which unit are dimensions usually given on technical drawings?
A scale of 2 : 1 means the drawing is twice as big as the real object.
Name the THREE views usually drawn in orthographic projection and say where each is placed in first-angle projection.
questions.memo:
✓ Front view: drawn first (1)
✓ Top view: below the front view (1)
✓ Left view: to the right of the front view (1)

questions.prompt: An electricity pylon is an example of a…
What type of structure is an egg?
Which is a solid structure?
Wind blowing against a building is a dynamic load.
Give THREE purposes of structures, with an example of each.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each, with example): support; protect; contain; span; shelter

questions.prompt: Explain why a car is a combination of structure types.
questions.memo:
✓ The chassis is a frame structure (1)
✓ The body is a thin shell structure (1)

questions.prompt: What is the method of adding diagonal members to make a frame rigid called?
Which makes a structure more stable?
options: A high centre of gravity and narrow base
A low centre of gravity and wide base

questions.prompt: Concrete is strong in tension but weak in compression.
Match each method to an example.

pairs.right: Triangular plate at a roof joint
Wire holding up a tent pole

questions.prompt: Explain why steel rods are placed in concrete beams.
questions.memo:
✓ Concrete is weak in tension (1)
✓ Steel is strong in tension, so it resists stretching in the beam (1)
